S1-B2.ruling: DISCHARGED against its discharged_when (each axis carries a disposition; trigger count recorded as an addition at :64-66). Two of the five grounds need correcting: R1 and R2 below.

axis_by_axis.event_type: True ground (:58). §11.2 requires a displayed minimum. With 139 types, picking that minimum after the result decides which types are shown, which is a real §8.5 concern. The 'no claim depends on it' reason also stands.
axis_by_axis.role: Acceptable descope with a stated reason (:59).
axis_by_axis.document_length_quartile: PARTIAL. 'Same ground as event type' (:60) does not carry over. Quartiles of 1,396 groups hold about 349 groups each, so no plausible displayed minimum excludes any of them, and the minimum-choice concern does not arise. The descope stands only on the second reason ('no claim depends on it; it cannot change a whole-split infeasibility'). See R2.
axis_by_axis.cross_sentence_distance: True (:61). Amendment 1:209-210, over all groups, exploratory.
axis_by_axis.seen_unseen_schema: PARTIAL. Checked against the plan text: the 'belongs to shift §10' ground has support in §10.3 (accepted-plan.md:430, 'seen versus unseen schema coverage' is a shift severity descriptor), in §3.4 item 2 (:132) and in Plan 1 §5 (docs/gate0/accepted-plan.md:194). But §11.2 (:464) lists the axis without restricting it to shift. The second sentence (:62), 'The certification split has no unseen-schema stratum to report', is a factual assertion with no cited evidence. It is not true by construction: the RAMS roles are a random grouped split (src/conformalextract/cli.py:98-102, train 0.45 / development 0.10 / certification 0.35 / final 0.10, seed 42), and the shift role is cross-dataset, so event-type or role combinations absent from train can occur in certification. See R1.
